"# ECHOES OF THE FALLEN
## A Detailed 2D Open-World Action RPG

Create a complete, highly polished, fully playable 2D action RPG titled \"ECHOES OF THE FALLEN\".

This must be a genuine 2D action RPG with detailed pixel art, real-time combat, exploration, character progression, quests, loot and a large interconnected world.

IMPORTANT: The game must prioritize gameplay depth, beautiful environments, smooth controls and satisfying combat.

Do NOT create a simple platformer, turn-based RPG, idle game or basic top-down walking simulator.

==================================================
1. GAME CONCEPT AND STORY
==================================================

The game takes place in a mysterious fantasy world called AETHERIA.

Long ago, the world was protected by ancient magical structures known as the Echo Monuments.

After a mysterious catastrophe, these structures became corrupted and strange creatures began appearing throughout the world.

Ancient settlements disappeared, forests became dangerous and forgotten civilizations were buried beneath the ruins.

The player controls a young wanderer who discovers an unusual connection to the ancient Echo Monuments.

Explore the world, discover forgotten civilizations, meet interesting characters, uncover hidden locations and gradually discover the truth behind the catastrophe.

Tell the story through exploration, dialogue, environmental storytelling and optional discoveries.

Avoid excessive cinematic cutscenes.

==================================================
2. ART STYLE AND GRAPHICS
==================================================

Create exceptionally detailed 2D pixel art.

Visual inspiration:
- Hyper Light Drifter.
- CrossCode.
- Eastward.
- Modern high-quality pixel-art RPGs.

The game must have:
- Detailed environmental tiles.
- Beautiful character sprites.
- Smooth character animations.
- Animated vegetation.
- Water reflections and movement.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Animated environmental particles.
- Beautiful spell effects.
- Detailed buildings and architecture.
- Distinctive enemy designs.

Use carefully designed pixel-art palettes.

Avoid generic flat-colored environments.

Make every region visually recognizable.

The world should feel handcrafted rather than randomly assembled.

==================================================
3. CAMERA AND WORLD VIEW
==================================================

Use a top-down camera with a slightly elevated perspective.

IMPORTANT:
The camera must show a relatively LARGE area around the player.

Use a wider camera view than typical zoomed-in RPG games.

The player should remain clearly visible while the camera shows surrounding terrain, enemies, paths and environmental details.

Implement smooth camera following.

Allow adjustable camera zoom in the settings.

Provide:
- Normal zoom.
- Wide zoom.
- Close zoom.

Default to a relatively wide view.

Do not make the world feel cramped.

==================================================
4. WORLD DESIGN
==================================================

Create a large interconnected fantasy world divided into distinct regions.

Initially implement these areas:

A. GREENFALL FOREST
- Dense forests.
- Ancient trees.
- Hidden paths.
- Small settlements.
- Abandoned shrines.
- Forest creatures.

B. THE FORGOTTEN KINGDOM
- Ruined castles.
- Old streets.
- Abandoned buildings.
- Ancient libraries.
- Hidden treasure rooms.

C. FROSTBOUND MOUNTAINS
- Snow-covered terrain.
- Frozen caves.
- Mountain paths.
- Ancient monuments.

D. THE SUNKEN DEPTHS
- Underground caverns.
- Glowing crystals.
- Ancient underground structures.
- Dangerous creatures.

E. THE CENTRAL SANCTUARY
- A peaceful settlement.
- Merchants.
- NPCs.
- Upgrade stations.
- Quest givers.
- A central hub for the player.

Make regions interconnected through paths, caves, gates and shortcuts.

Some locations should require progression or special abilities to access.

Use a consistent world map.

==================================================
5. PLAYER CHARACTER
==================================================

Create a detailed animated pixel-art protagonist.

The player should have:
- Idle animation.
- Walking animation.
- Running animation.
- Dodge animation.
- Attack animation.
- Casting animation.
- Damage animation.

Allow the player to customize:
- Outfit colors.
- Cosmetic accessories.
- Appearance details.

Make the protagonist visually recognizable.

==================================================
6. REAL-TIME COMBAT
==================================================

Combat is one of the most important aspects of this game.

It must feel responsive, fluid and satisfying.

Implement:
- Fast basic attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Combos.
- Dodging.
- Blocking or defensive abilities.
- Magical abilities.
- Area-of-effect attacks.
- Cooldowns.
- Stamina or energy management.

Create several distinct magical abilities:

1. ARCANE BURST
A fast magical projectile.

2. BLINK
A short-distance movement ability that avoids incoming attacks.

3. NOVA
An area attack surrounding the player.

4. FROST BIND
Temporarily slows nearby enemies.

5. ECHO STRIKE
A powerful ability that releases stored magical energy.

Allow abilities to be unlocked and upgraded.

Make combat skill-based rather than button-mashing.

Use clear visual feedback for hits, dodges, enemy attacks and ability activation.

==================================================
7. ENEMIES AND BOSSES
==================================================

Create diverse enemy types.

Examples:
- Small forest creatures.
- Fast aggressive enemies.
- Armored guardians.
- Ranged magical creatures.
- Large elite monsters.
- Ancient corrupted guardians.

Each enemy should have distinct behavior.

Implement:
- Patrol.
- Detection.
- Chasing.
- Attacking.
- Dodging or repositioning.
- Taking damage.
- Defeat animations.

Create several boss encounters.

Bosses should have:
- Unique visual designs.
- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different combat phases.
- Clearly telegraphed attacks.
- Distinctive arenas.
- Rewarding victory sequences.

Boss fights should require learning attack patterns.

==================================================
8. RPG PROGRESSION
==================================================

Create a meaningful character progression system.

Include:
- Character level.
- Experience points.
- Health.
- Energy.
- Stamina.
- Attack power.
- Defense.
- Movement speed.

Enemies and quests reward experience.

Leveling up grants progression points.

Create a skill tree with three branches:

ARCANE:
Focus on magical damage and elemental abilities.

MOBILITY:
Focus on movement, dodging and speed.

GUARDIAN:
Focus on defense, survivability and counterattacks.

Allow players to choose their preferred playstyle.

==================================================
9. LOOT AND EQUIPMENT
==================================================

Create a rewarding loot system.

Item rarities:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.

Add collectible:
- Magical crystals.
- Ancient relics.
- Crafting materials.
- Healing supplies.
- Upgrade components.
- Cosmetic items.

Equipment should have meaningful statistics and visual differences.

Allow the player to inspect, compare and equip discovered items.

Add an inventory with limited space.

Include equipment management and item sorting.

==================================================
10. QUESTS AND NPCS
==================================================

Create a variety of quests.

Main quests:
- Discover ancient monuments.
- Investigate corrupted regions.
- Find missing explorers.
- Recover forgotten artifacts.

Side quests:
- Help villagers.
- Find lost objects.
- Explore hidden locations.
- Defeat dangerous creatures.
- Discover secret areas.

NPCs should have individual dialogue and useful information.

Create a simple quest journal.

Clearly display current objectives.

Avoid repetitive fetch quests as the only form of content.

==================================================
11. EXPLORATION AND SECRETS
==================================================

Exploration should be rewarding.

Add:
- Hidden caves.
- Secret rooms.
- Treasure chests.
- Optional boss encounters.
- Ancient puzzles.
- Hidden shortcuts.
- Rare collectible objects.
- Environmental storytelling.

Allow the player to discover things naturally without constantly following quest markers.

Create a minimap and a larger world map.

Show discovered and undiscovered areas differently.

==================================================
12. MOBILE AND DESKTOP CONTROLS
==================================================

Desktop:
- WASD or arrow keys: movement.
- Mouse or keyboard: combat abilities.
- Space: dodge.
- E: interaction.
- I: inventory.
- M: map.
- Escape: pause.

Mobile:
- Left virtual joystick.
- Dedicated attack button.
- Dodge button.
- Three or four ability buttons.
- Interaction button.
- Inventory and map buttons.

Make all mobile controls responsive.

Allow adjustable button sizes and positions if practical.

Support landscape mobile orientation.

Do not let the interface obstruct the gameplay.

==================================================
13. USER INTERFACE
==================================================

Create a beautiful fantasy RPG interface.

During gameplay display:
- Health bar.
- Energy bar.
- Experience bar.
- Character level.
- Current objective.
- Ability cooldowns.
- Minimap.

Create separate interfaces for:
- Main menu.
- Inventory.
- Character stats.
- Skill tree.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Equipment.
- Settings.

Use a consistent visual design.

Make menus readable and attractive.

==================================================
14. AUDIO AND ATMOSPHERE
==================================================

Include atmospheric music and sound effects if possible.

Examples:
- Forest ambience.
- Wind.
- Water.
- Footsteps.
- Combat sounds.
- Magical effects.
- Enemy sounds.
- Environmental interaction sounds.
- Menu sounds.

Use lightweight synthesized audio or small assets.

Include separate music and sound effect volume controls.

==================================================
15. GRAPHICS SETTINGS
==================================================

Include a functional settings menu.

Graphics options:
- Low.
- Medium.
- High.

Allow adjustment of:
- Particle effects.
- Environmental effects.
- Shadows or lighting effects.
- Screen shake.
- Camera zoom.

Include an FPS-friendly mode.

Settings must actually affect rendering and performance.

==================================================
16. SAVE SYSTEM
==================================================

Implement automatic local saving.

Save:
- Character level.
- Experience.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Unlocked abilities.
- Quest progress.
- Discovered regions.
- Collected items.
- Settings.

Use localStorage or IndexedDB.

The game must preserve progress after refreshing the browser.

==================================================
17. TECHNICAL AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

This game must remain lightweight.

Prefer Phaser 3 or a suitable 2D Canvas rendering framework.

Requirements:
- Genuine 2D rendering.
- No unnecessary 3D rendering.
- Efficient tilemap rendering.
- Reusable sprites and animations.
- Texture atlases where useful.
- Object pooling for particles.
- Efficient enemy updates.
- Limited simultaneous effects.
- Responsive rendering.
- Mobile browser support.
- Desktop browser support.
- No mandatory external API.
- No paid API dependencies.

Avoid excessively large assets.

Generate procedural effects when appropriate.

Optimize for mid-range Android phones.

==================================================
18. DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY
==================================================

Build the game in stages.

STAGE 1:
Create the main character, detailed environment, movement, camera and mobile controls.

STAGE 2:
Implement real-time combat, abilities, enemies and health.

STAGE 3:
Create the first explorable region, loot, inventory and basic progression.

STAGE 4:
Add quests, NPCs, world map and additional areas.

STAGE 5:
Implement bosses, skill tree, equipment and advanced progression.

STAGE 6:
Polish graphics, animations, sound and settings.

After each stage, test existing functionality.

Do not attempt to generate an enormous unfinished world in one step.

Prioritize a small but complete playable experience before expanding.

==================================================
19. FINAL QUALITY EXPECTATIONS
==================================================

The finished game should feel like a genuine indie action RPG.

It must have:
- Beautiful detailed pixel art.
- A relatively wide camera view.
- Responsive real-time combat.
- Smooth animations.
- Interesting enemies.
- Meaningful progression.
- Rewarding exploration.
- A functional inventory.
- A satisfying RPG gameplay loop.
- Excellent mobile controls.

Do not create fake buttons or decorative systems that do nothing.

Do not claim features are implemented unless they actually work.

The first playable build should contain one complete region, several enemies, one boss, collectible items, a working progression system and a save system.

Make the game fun to play before expanding its world.

The final result should be visually impressive, lightweight, atmospheric and genuinely enjoyable.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Item rarities:

- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.

Add collectible:
- Magical crystals.
- Ancient relics.
- Crafting materials.
- Healing supplies.
- Upgrade components.
- Cosmetic items.

Equipment should have meaningful statistics and visual differences.

Allow the player to inspect, compare and equip discovered items.

Add an inventory with limited space.

Include equipment management and item sorting.

==================================================
10. QUESTS AND NPCS
==================================================

Create a variety of quests.

Main quests:
- Discover ancient monuments.
- Investigate corrupted regions.
- Find missing explorers.
- Recover forgotten artifacts.

Side quests:
- Help villagers.
- Find lost objects.
- Explore hidden locations.
- Defeat dangerous creatures.
- Discover secret areas.

NPCs should have individual dialogue and useful information.

Create a simple quest journal.

Clearly display current objectives.

Avoid repetitive fetch quests as the only form of content.

==================================================
11. EXPLORATION AND SECRETS
==================================================

Exploration should be rewarding.

Add:
- Hidden caves.
- Secret rooms.
- Treasure chests.
- Optional boss encounters.
- Ancient puzzles.
- Hidden shortcuts.
- Rare collectible objects.
- Environmental storytelling.

Allow the player to discover things naturally without constantly following quest markers.

Create a minimap and a larger world map.

Show discovered and undiscovered areas differently.

==================================================
12. MOBILE AND DESKTOP CONTROLS
==================================================

Desktop:
- WASD or arrow keys: movement.
- Mouse or keyboard: combat abilities.
- Space: dodge.
- E: interaction.
- I: inventory.
- M: map.
- Escape: pause.

Mobile:
- Left virtual joystick.
- Dedicated attack button.
- Dodge button.
- Three or four ability buttons.
- Interaction button.
- Inventory and map buttons.

Make all mobile controls responsive.

Allow adjustable button sizes and positions if practical.

Support landscape mobile orientation.

Do not let the interface obstruct the gameplay.

==================================================
13. USER INTERFACE
==================================================

Create a beautiful fantasy RPG interface.

During gameplay display:
- Health bar.
- Energy bar.
- Experience bar.
- Character level.
- Current objective.
- Ability cooldowns.
- Minimap.

Create separate interfaces for:
- Main menu.
- Inventory.
- Character stats.
- Skill tree.
- Quest journal.
- World map.
- Equipment.
- Settings.

Use a consistent visual design.

Make menus readable and attractive.

==================================================
14. AUDIO AND ATMOSPHERE
==================================================

Include atmospheric music and sound effects if possible.

Examples:
- Forest ambience.
- Wind.
- Water.
- Footsteps.
- Combat sounds.
- Magical effects.
- Enemy sounds.
- Environmental interaction sounds.
- Menu sounds.

Use lightweight synthesized audio or small assets.

Include separate music and sound effect volume controls.

==================================================
15. GRAPHICS SETTINGS
==================================================

Include a functional settings menu.

Graphics options:
- Low.
- Medium.
- High.

Allow adjustment of:
- Particle effects.
- Environmental effects.
- Shadows or lighting effects.
- Screen shake.
- Camera zoom.

Include an FPS-friendly mode.

Settings must actually affect rendering and performance.

==================================================
16. SAVE SYSTEM
==================================================

Implement automatic local saving.

Save:
- Character level.
- Experience.
- Inventory.
- Equipment.
- Unlocked abilities.
- Quest progress.
- Discovered regions.
- Collected items.
- Settings.

Use localStorage or IndexedDB.

The game must preserve progress after refreshing the browser.

==================================================
17. TECHNICAL AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

This game must remain lightweight.

Prefer Phaser 3 or a suitable 2D Canvas rendering framework.

Requirements:
- Genuine 2D rendering.
- No unnecessary 3D rendering.
- Efficient tilemap rendering.
- Reusable sprites and animations.
- Texture atlases where useful.
- Object pooling for particles.
- Efficient enemy updates.
- Limited simultaneous effects.
- Responsive rendering.
- Mobile browser support.
- Desktop browser support.
- No mandatory external API.
- No paid API dependencies.

Avoid excessively large assets.

Generate procedural effects when appropriate.

Optimize for mid-range Android phones.

==================================================
18. DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY
==================================================

Build the game in stages.

STAGE 1:
Create the main character, detailed environment, movement, camera and mobile controls.

STAGE 2:
Implement real-time combat, abilities, enemies and health.

STAGE 3:
Create the first explorable region, loot, inventory and basic progression.

STAGE 4:
Add quests, NPCs, world map and additional areas.

STAGE 5:
Implement bosses, skill tree, equipment and advanced progression.

STAGE 6:
Polish graphics, animations, sound and settings.

After each stage, test existing functionality.

Do not attempt to generate an enormous unfinished world in one step.

Prioritize a small but complete playable experience before expanding.

==================================================
19. FINAL QUALITY EXPECTATIONS
==================================================

The finished game should feel like a genuine indie action RPG.

It must have:
- Beautiful detailed pixel art.
- A relatively wide camera view.
- Responsive real-time combat.
- Smooth animations.
- Interesting enemies.
- Meaningful progression.
- Rewarding exploration.
- A functional inventory.
- A satisfying RPG gameplay loop.
- Excellent mobile controls.

Do not create fake buttons or decorative systems that do nothing.

Do not claim features are implemented unless they actually work.

The first playable build should contain one complete region, several enemies, one boss, collectible items, a working progression system and a save system.

Make the game fun to play before expanding its world.

The final result should be visually impressive, lightweight, atmospheric and genuinely enjoyable.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
